item.title: The Skis That Came in from the Cold - Secrets of the Ice
item.description: Melting of the high mountain ice has released a number of ancient skis. They shed important new light on the earliest history of skiing.

item.title: Buried in Ice - The Franklin Expedition Cemetery - Secrets of the Ice
item.description: We take a closer look at the Beechey Island permafrost burials. What can they tell us about the disastrous Franklin expedition?

item.title: Reidar Marstein - Our Local Hero of Glacier Archaeology - Secrets of the Ice
item.description: Reidar Marstein is a core member of the Secrets of the Ice team. Without him, glacial archaeology in Oppland would have looked very different.

item.title: The Hunt for the Lost Mountain Pass - Secrets of the Ice
item.description: When the fog lifted, we saw that the ground around us was littered with artifacts. We had found a lost mountain pass. the discovery of a lifetime.

item.title: Prehistoric Arrow Bonanza at Langfonne - Secrets of the Ice
item.description: We discovered an archaeological ice site with record-breaking numbesr of prehistoric arrows. But how do we get from arrow to history?

item.title: The Lost Viking Settlement - Secrets of the Ice
item.description: The path from the Lendbreen pass led us to another fantastic discovery – a lost Viking settlement in the mountains. First results are in.

item.title: The Best-Preserved Pair of Skis from Prehistory - Secrets of the Ice
item.description: We have found the best-preserved paIr of skis from prehistory at the Digervarden ice patch in Norway. They are 1300 years old.

item.title: Finding and Documenting Glacial Archaeological Sites - Secrets of the Ice
item.description: We tell the story of how we find and document glacial archaeological sites in Innlandet County, Norway, based of 15 years of experience.

item.title: Ötzi – a new understanding of the holy grail of glacial archaeology - Secrets of the Ice
item.description: Ötzi is the star of glacial archaeology. Incredibly, the ice mummy and his artefacts were only preserved by a string of lucky coincidences. Really?

item.title: Secrets of the Ice Wins Europe’s Top Heritage Award - Secrets of the Ice
item.description: We are thrilled to announce that Secrets of the Ice has received the 2025 European Heritage Award / Europa Nostra Award in the Research category.
